```{r setup, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
project.folder <- paste0(here::here(), "/")
source(paste0(project.folder, "create_folder_structure.R"))
source(paste0(functions.folder, "script_initiate.R"))
suppressMessages({library(flextable); library(officer); library(knitr); library(kableExtra)
                  library(INLA); library(Matrix)})
INLA::inla.setOption(num.threads = 2)
set.seed(20260911); NBOOT <- 2000

source(paste0(functions.folder, "table_helpers.R"))
# the shared helper takes an output folder; everything here goes to the same place
.tw <- to_word
to_word <- function(dt, name, ...) .tw(dt, name, tables_main_folder, ...)
```

```{r data}
panel <- setDT(readRDS(paste0(objects_folder, multistate_ts_daily_rds)))
panel[, date := as.Date(date)]
cc <- setDT(readRDS(paste0(objects_folder, "case_crossover_df_shock_post7.RDS")))
if (anyDuplicated(names(cc))) cc <- cc[, which(!duplicated(names(cc))), with = FALSE]
cases <- cc[outbreak_binary == 1]
shock <- setDT(readRDS(paste0(objects_folder, "daily_shock_predictors.RDS")))
shock[, date := as.Date(date)]
clim <- rbindlist(lapply(
  list.files(env_data, pattern = "flyway8_climatology_1997_2021_w", full.names = TRUE),
  fread, colClasses = list(character = "zone_id")))
STATE_ORD <- cases[, .N, by = state][order(-N)]$state
```

## Table 1. Case-crossover sample by state

```{r table1}
SEAS4 <- c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall")
# Describes the analytic sample itself - cases, the cells they sit in, and the referent
# person-time each case is compared against. Land cover was dropped: it is a property of the
# cell, and a case-crossover compares a cell against itself, so it can never enter the model.
per_cell <- cases[, .(n = .N), by = .(state, zone_id)]
samp <- cc[, .(events = sum(outbreak_binary), refs = sum(outbreak_binary == 0),
               total = .N), by = state]
samp[, per := sprintf("%.0f", refs / events)]   # a count of days, so no decimal
cells <- per_cell[, .(c1 = .N, c2 = sum(n >= 2), c3 = sum(n >= 3)), by = state]
sea <- dcast(cases[, .N, by = .(state, season)], state ~ season, value.var = "N", fill = 0)
for (sn in SEAS4) if (!sn %in% names(sea)) set(sea, j = sn, value = 0L)
sea[, tot := rowSums(.SD), .SDcols = SEAS4]
for (sn in SEAS4) set(sea, j = paste0(sn, "_f"),
                      value = sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", sea[[sn]], 100 * sea[[sn]] / sea$tot))

fmt_n <- function(x) formatC(x, big.mark = ",", format = "d")
grab <- function(dt, v, f) setNames(f(dt[[v]][match(STATE_ORD, dt$state)]), STATE_ORD)
blank <- setNames(rep("", length(STATE_ORD)), STATE_ORD)
hdr <- function(lab) as.list(c(Variable = lab, blank))
row <- function(lab, dt, v, f = fmt_n) as.list(c(Variable = lab, grab(dt, v, f)))

# Section headers carry their own total rather than sitting empty above a row that repeats it:
# "Case cells" IS the count of cells with at least one event, and "Cases" IS the event count.
t1 <- rbindlist(list(
  row("Cases", samp, "events"),
    row("Winter", sea, "Winter_f", as.character),
    row("Spring", sea, "Spring_f", as.character),
    row("Summer", sea, "Summer_f", as.character),
    row("Fall",   sea, "Fall_f",   as.character),
  row("Case cells", cells, "c1"),
    row("With 2 or more events", cells, "c2"),
    row("With 3 or more events", cells, "c3"),
  row("Referent cell-days", samp, "refs"),
    row("Referents per case", samp, "per", as.character),
  row("Total cell-days", samp, "total")), fill = TRUE)

T1HDR  <- c(1, 6, 9, 11)                   # rows that head a block and carry its total
T1BODY <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(t1)), T1HDR)
T1TITLE <- "Table 1. Case-crossover sample by state"
T1NOTE  <- paste("Cells are 10 km grid squares. Referent cell-days are the other days in the same",
                 "calendar month within the same cell, excluding the 7 days after detection.")
to_word(t1, "Table1_case_crossover_sample", indent_rows = T1BODY, bold_rows = T1HDR,
        rule_after = c(5, 8, 10), title = T1TITLE, note = T1NOTE)
show_tbl(t1, indent_rows = T1BODY, bold_rows = T1HDR, title = T1TITLE, note = T1NOTE)
```

## Table 2. Minnesota, by meteorological season

```{r table2}
SEASONS <- c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall")
COLS    <- c(SEASONS, "Year-round")
# ERA5 gives Kelvin and metres. Levels need converting; DIFFERENCES do not for temperature
# (a Kelvin difference is a Celsius difference), and the precipitation shock is a log ratio
# because a_07 log1p-transforms it before differencing.
nat <- function(x, v) {
  if (v == "temperature")        x - 273.15
  else if (v == "precipitation") x * 1000
  else if (v == "soil_moisture") x * 100      # m3/m3 -> % volumetric, so no 3-decimal cells
  else                           x
}
natd <- function(x, v) {
  if (v == "precipitation")      (exp(x) - 1) * 100
  else if (v == "soil_moisture") x * 100
  else                           x
}

MET <- c(temperature = "Temperature (°C)", precipitation = "Precipitation (mm)",
         soil_moisture = "Soil moisture (% vol)", wind_speed = "Wind speed (m/s)")
DEPU <- c(temperature = "°C", precipitation = "% vs baseline",
          soil_moisture = "% volumetric", wind_speed = "m/s")
BIRD <- c(anseriformes = "Anseriformes", predators = "Predators")

season_table <- function(case_cells) {
  d <- panel[zone_id %in% case_cells]
  d <- merge(d, shock, by = c("zone_id", "date"), all.x = TRUE)
  d[, week_idx := pmin(as.integer(strftime(date, "%j")) %/% 7L, 51L)]
  d <- merge(d, clim[, c("zone_id", "week_idx", grep("_mean$", names(clim), value = TRUE)),
                     with = FALSE], by = c("zone_id", "week_idx"), all.x = TRUE)
  d[, season := factor(season, levels = SEASONS)]
  d[, week_blk := strftime(date, "%Y-%V")]   # resampling unit for the interval
  ev <- cases[zone_id %in% case_cells]

  # one column per season, one value per cell, and the ROW LABEL says which statistic it is.
  # levels get median (IQR); the 25-year comparison gets median (95% CrI), because a spread is
  # not what that row is claiming - it is a difference from a normal, so it needs an interval on
  # the estimate rather than a description of the scatter.
  ms <- function(x, dp) sprintf(paste0("%.", dp, "f (%.", dp, "f, %.", dp, "f)"),
                                median(x, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(x, .25, na.rm = TRUE),
                                quantile(x, .75, na.rm = TRUE))
  # MEDIAN deviation from the 25-year normal, with a credible interval from INLA.
  #
  # AR1, NOT a random walk. RW1 is non-stationary: it absorbs the whole weather trajectory into
  # the smooth and leaves the intercept pinned down by residual noise, giving a 0.17-wide
  # interval on a quantity whose real uncertainty is ~5. AR1 is stationary - autocorrelated
  # noise AROUND a mean - so the correlation properly inflates that mean's uncertainty.
  #
  # Fitted on DAY MEDIANS, so it matches the median (IQR) used everywhere else in the table
  # rather than mixing a mean into a median column. Cells are collapsed to one median per day
  # first: all cells sit under the same weather on a given day (cell means SD 0.38 vs day means
  # 4.67), so they are near-replicates, and the day is the unit that actually carries the
  # uncertainty. The AR1 intercept is then the central level of that daily-median series.
  mci <- function(x, day, dp) {
    keep <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(day); x <- x[keep]; day <- day[keep]
    if (!length(x)) return("")
    dm <- data.table(y = x, d = day)[, .(y = median(y, na.rm = TRUE)), by = d][order(d)]
    if (nrow(dm) < 10) return(sprintf(paste0("%.", dp, "f"), median(x, na.rm = TRUE)))
    dm[, t := .I]
    f <- try(INLA::inla(y ~ 1 + f(t, model = "ar1"), family = "gaussian", data = dm,
                        control.predictor = list(compute = FALSE)), silent = TRUE)
    if (inherits(f, "try-error")) return("")
    b <- f$summary.fixed["(Intercept)", c("mean", "0.025quant", "0.975quant")]
    sprintf(paste0("%.", dp, "f (%.", dp, "f, %.", dp, "f)"), b[[1]], b[[2]], b[[3]])
  }
  # "Year-round" is every case-cell day, not the average of the four seasons
  mkrow <- function(lab, f) as.list(c(Variable = lab,
    setNames(vapply(COLS, function(s) f(if (s == "Year-round") d else d[season == s]),
                    character(1)), COLS)))

  rows <- list(
    as.list(c(Variable = "Case cells",
              setNames(vapply(COLS, function(s) as.character(
                uniqueN((if (s == "Year-round") ev else ev[season == s])$zone_id)),
                character(1)), COLS))),
    as.list(c(Variable = "Spillover events",
              setNames(vapply(COLS, function(s) as.character(
                nrow(if (s == "Year-round") ev else ev[season == s])), character(1)), COLS))))
  for (v in names(MET)) {
    dp  <- 1
    dpd <- if (v == "precipitation") 0 else 1
    rows <- c(rows, list(
      mkrow(paste0(MET[[v]], ", median (IQR)"), function(ds) ms(nat(ds[[v]], v), dp)),
      mkrow("vs 25-yr normal, median (95% CrI)",
            function(ds) mci(nat(ds[[v]], v) - nat(ds[[paste0(v, "_mean")]], v), ds$date, dp))))
  }
  for (v in names(BIRD))
    rows <- c(rows, list(mkrow(paste0(BIRD[[v]], ", median (IQR)"), function(ds) ms(ds[[v]], 1))))
  rbindlist(rows, fill = TRUE)
}

t2 <- season_table(unique(cases[state == "Minnesota"]$zone_id))
IND  <- c(4, 6, 8, 10)                     # the 25-year row sits under its exposure
BOLD <- c(3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 12)
RULE <- c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10)
to_word(t2, "Table2_minnesota_by_season", indent_rows = IND, bold_rows = BOLD,
        rule_after = RULE, sig = TRUE,
        title = "Table 2. Conditions in Minnesota spillover cells, by meteorological season",
        note = "Summarised over all cell-days in the 73 Minnesota cells with at least one spillover. Deviations are from the 1997-2021 weekly normal for that cell, reported as the median across cells with a 95% credible interval from an INLA AR(1) model over day. CrI = credible interval; IQR = interquartile range.")
show_tbl(t2, indent_rows = IND, bold_rows = BOLD, sig = TRUE,
         title = "Table 2. Conditions in Minnesota spillover cells, by meteorological season",
         note = "Summarised over all cell-days in the 73 Minnesota cells with at least one spillover. Deviations are from the 1997-2021 weekly normal for that cell, reported as the median across cells with a 95% credible interval from an INLA AR(1) model over day. CrI = credible interval; IQR = interquartile range.")
```
